comments.body:
## Decision material for refuse-vs-redact — measured, not argued

This ticket's plan says "rejects (or redacts, per config)". That ambiguity is load-bearing and
blocks implementation, so here is the evidence an operator needs to rule.

## The write boundary

`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:349` `append_event(...)` is the single seam every event write
passes through. A screen has exactly one place to live, which is good news for either option.

## The false-positive population is REAL, and it is almost entirely self-referential

Swept all 3,299 ticket dirs for `sk-ant-api03`. Five files match. NONE is a credential:

    jira-reb-687/...-REVIEW_RESULT.json   (x2)  LLM review output DESCRIBING the pattern
    .bridge_state/bindings.json                 reconciler state cache
    e7a9-.../...-CREATE.json                    THIS TICKET'S OWN DESCRIPTION
    e7a9-.../...-EDIT.json                      THIS TICKET, EDITED

Actual matched content, verbatim:

    sk-ant-api03-...'), Bearer headers, and request-body
    sk-ant-api03-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{93,}) and Bearer token pa

Both are a truncated placeholder and a REGEX LITERAL, in prose describing the screen.

Zero matches for `ghp_`-shaped strings anywhere in the store.

## The finding that should drive the decision

**A naive refuse-on-write screen would have refused the creation of this very ticket.** Two of
the five matches are e7a9's own CREATE and EDIT events. Any agent writing up a credential
incident, filing a bug about a leak, or pasting a detection regex into a plan hits the screen
while doing exactly the right thing.

So the screen's hard problem is not detection sensitivity. It is distinguishing a LIVE credential
from a DESCRIPTION of one — and the corpus says descriptions are the common case by a wide
margin. Today they are 5 of 5.

## What that implies for each option

REFUSE (fail the write):
+ Strongest guarantee; a secret cannot enter the append-only store, which is the whole point,
  since the store auto-pushes and a leak wedges the entire tickets branch behind GitHub push
  protection.
- Hard-fails an agent mid-operation. Given the corpus, the FIRST failures in practice would
  likely be agents writing about security, i.e. it fires hardest on the work it is meant to
  protect. Needs the escape hatch to be excellent, and the ticket explicitly says
  `--allow-secret-pattern` must NOT be exposed over MCP.

REDACT (scrub and continue):
+ No workflow interruption; benign look-alikes survive as-is if the pattern is precise.
- Silently MUTATES an event body, which cuts against the store's append-only audit properties.
  A reader cannot distinguish "this text never contained a secret" from "this text was scrubbed",
  unless the redaction is itself recorded as an event — which is a design question the ticket
  does not currently answer.

## A third option the ticket does not currently name

REFUSE ONLY HIGH-CONFIDENCE LIVE SHAPES, WARN ON THE REST. The two are distinguishable more
easily than the ticket assumes: a live Anthropic key is a fixed-length high-entropy string
(`{93,}` per the regex already in the corpus), whereas every current false positive is either
truncated (`sk-ant-api03-...`) or a bracket-expression regex. Length plus an entropy floor
separates them without needing to understand intent.

This may be the cheapest path to a screen that is safe to leave ON by default, which the ticket's
AC3 explicitly requires ("benign look-alike text is not refused ... so the screen is safe to
leave on by default").

## What is NOT yet determined

- Whether `.bridge_state/bindings.json` matches for a benign reason or is a genuine finding. It
  is a reconciler state cache, not a ticket event; someone should look before assuming.
- The false-positive rate for shapes OTHER than `sk-ant-api03` (AWS keys, Bearer tokens,
  `ghp_`). Only the Anthropic shape was swept here; `ghp_` returned zero.
- Whether the redaction-as-event approach has precedent in this store's schema.

comments.body:
OPERATOR DECISION (2026-08-07): REFUSE, with an allowed force override.

On detecting a secret in an event body at the append_event seam, the write is REFUSED — the event does not land. A force override is available for the operator judgment call (same escape-hatch shape as --force-close), so a false positive can never permanently block a legitimate write.

This settles the refuse-vs-redact question that was blocking implementation. Redaction is NOT adopted: silently rewriting a caller's payload makes the stored event differ from what the caller believes it wrote, and in an event-sourced store that divergence is unrecoverable after the fact. Refusing is loud, reversible, and leaves the caller in control.

Implementation notes implied by the decision:
- refusal must name WHICH detector fired and where, so the override is an informed choice rather than a blind retry;
- the refusal path must not itself echo the secret into stderr or logs;
- the override must be recorded on the event (who forced, why) so a forced write is auditable rather than indistinguishable from a clean one.

This also discharges the dependency noted on 2a76 AC5, which was marked [operator-attested] pending exactly this ruling.

comments.body:
## Incident record — blast radius (AC8)

**What happened.** 2026-08-03 19:13, a session posted a comment on ticket 129e whose body
was a full zsh environment dump. The dump embedded SEVEN live credentials: Anthropic, two
GitHub PATs, Gemini/Google, Jira/Atlassian, an OpenAI service-account key, and a PyPI token.

**Mechanism.** The body was produced by an unquoted shell command substitution. The shell
expanded it before rebar saw anything, so rebar received an ordinary string and — having no
write-time screen at `append_event` — wrote it. The store auto-pushes, so the comment was
published on the next push attempt.

**Blast radius.** GitHub push protection rejected `refs/heads/tickets` (GH013) on the
Anthropic key. Because rebar's tickets branch is a single shared ref, EVERY session's store
writes then queued local-only — 153 commits at diagnosis. This was a full store-sharing
outage for all concurrent agents, caused by one comment, and it presented as transient
contention rather than as a leak: the only symptom was
`WARNING rebar._store.push: tickets branch push failed after 3 retries`.

**The control that actually stopped the leak was OUTSIDE this project.** Nothing in rebar
detected, refused, or reported the credentials. GitHub push protection did — and it did so
by breaking the store for everyone, which is the loudest possible failure mode and the least
useful one. That is the gap this ticket closes: the same refusal, moved to the write seam,
where it costs one command instead of the whole branch.

**Secondary defect, already fixed elsewhere.** The push-retry path swallowed the git stderr,
so the outage did not self-identify. That was bug 2a76 (`test_push_rejection_surfacing.py`),
which landed the GH013 reason + unpushed backlog into the warning. AC3 and its half of AC4
are therefore already satisfied on main; this change does not duplicate them.

comments.body:
## Implementation landed in a worktree — mechanism, decisions, and what the review found

### Proven mechanism (RED before GREEN)

Confirmed by a failing test before any fix: `leaf.comment(<ticket>, "KEY=<live-shaped
anthropic key>")` returned 0 and the COMMENT event landed on disk. There was no content
screening anywhere in the write path — `_store/event_append._validate_event` checks the
envelope shape and `event_type` membership only, and never inspects `data`.

### The seam is NOT `append_event` — that was the important correction

The ticket and the earlier decision comment both name `append_event` as the single seam. It
is not. An adversarial review of the change found four writers that reach the store without
it, and one of them matters a lot: `_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate` writes
Jira-sourced COMMENT/EDIT bodies — untrusted external input — by calling the two halves of
`finalize_event` directly. A screen in `append_event` would have left a credential pasted
into a Jira comment able to reproduce the exact wedge this ticket exists to prevent.

The screen therefore lives in `_seam.finalize_event`, which `append_event`, the txn and
delete cores, and (now) the reconciler all route through. A test pins the reconciler's
routing so it cannot regress back into a bypass.

### The no-echo property, and how it is tested

`SecretFinding(family, field, line)` has no value field — structurally, not by convention.
Payload dict KEYS are redacted before they reach the field path (a review finding: the path
is printed by the refusal, so a credential used as a key was a leak channel). The test
asserts the value AND its head/tail fragments are absent from five channels: the exception
message, stdout, stderr, the log records, and every byte on disk. The forced-write path —
the only path that logs — is checked separately, since the refusal path emits no records and
that assertion would otherwise be vacuous. A positive control proves the on-disk check
actually observes landed values.

### Detection tuned by measurement, not by argument

Two fail-open bugs the review caught, both fixed:

* **Padding defeated the entropy floor.** With greedy `{80,}` quantifiers, entropy was
  computed over the whole match, so appending same-class padding after a real key — 400 `-`
  characters, i.e. an ASCII rule in a log or env dump — dragged the average under the floor
  and the screen MISSED a genuine credential. Patterns now match a fixed-width window, so
  nothing appended after a key can dilute it.
* **The PEM pattern fired on prose.** Line-anchored now: a real paste puts the header on its
  own line; a ticket enumerating headers in backticks does not.

Measured false-positive rate against the LIVE store (25,125 events swept with the shipped
patterns): **1**, and it is `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` — AWS's own published doc example, quoted
in a ticket about secret scanning. Recoverable via the override. Zero hits across this repo's
own docs and source. That is the evidence for AC "safe to leave on by default".

### The override

`--allow-secret-pattern=<reason>` is parsed above BOTH dispatch routes, so every write verb
honours it — not just `comment`. The review found the first cut advertised an override in the
refusal message that did not exist for `create`/`edit`/`session-log`, which would have made a
false positive on a description a permanent hard block. Only the `--flag=<reason>` form is
accepted (a reason cannot be omitted), the pre-`--` segment only (so a body that legitimately
begins with the flag still writes verbatim), and the reason + bypassed families are recorded
on the event itself. CLI-only; a test pins its absence from the MCP surface.

### Reuse

`llm/workflow/lint.py` now consumes the shared pattern table rather than keeping its own,
which had already drifted — it lacked the Anthropic/OpenAI/Atlassian/PyPI families the leak
actually carried.

### AC status

AC3 (push failures logging the GH013 reason) and its half of AC4 were already satisfied on
main by bug 2a76 (`tests/unit/test_push_rejection_surfacing.py`); not duplicated. AC7 is
`docs/user-guide.md` — the command-substitution hazard, with the exact wrong and right forms.
AC8 is the incident-record comment above.

Two adjacent concerns are filed as 4802 (`discovered_from` e7a9): the LLM sidecars swallow a
screen refusal, and inbound reconcile now fails an event loudly on a Jira-sourced secret.

comments.body:
## Review-gate remediation for Gerrit 1490 — both blocking findings closed

Patch Set 1 drew `LLM-Review -1` on two blocking findings. Both are now remediated (PS2,
`bd57f939a2`). Recording the evidence, because one part of it changes how this repo should
handle this class of false positive in future.

### Finding 1 — `secret-detection` (2 matches on changed files)

The deterministic detector is **gitleaks**, auto-discovering `.gitleaks.toml` from the scan root
(`src/rebar/grounding/engine_b.py::_run_sarif`, which passes no `--config` override). Reproduced
locally against the PS1 tree: exactly 2 matches, both rule `private-key`, both **confirmed false
positives** — neither carries key material:

1. `src/rebar/secret_screen.py` — the pattern-table comment quoting a PEM begin-banner in prose
   to explain why the shipped pattern is line-anchored. The shipped regex itself does not match
   (it contains a character class); only the prose did.
2. `tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py` — the positive-control fixture, whose "body" is a
   15-character base64 stub that decodes to the ASCII text `openssh-key`.

No real secret was present. Nothing was weakened or deleted to clear them.

### The measurement that decided the remedy — an allowlist here would have been a FAIL-OPEN

The obvious remedy was `.gitleaks.toml`, this repo's sanctioned allowlist (it already exempts the
Langfuse docker-compose throwaways and the `test-signing-key-` fixtures). That was drafted, then
**rejected on measurement**. Experiment: append a throwaway `openssl genrsa` key to each file and
re-scan.

| file | allowlist entry keyed on… | real key appended → |
|---|---|---|
| `src/rebar/secret_screen.py` | the banner followed by a backtick (prose only) | **DETECTED** |
| `tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py` | the fixture's fake body | **MISSED** |

Once the FIRST `private-key` match in a file is suppressed by an allowlist, gitleaks does not go
on to report a genuine key later in that same file. So an allowlist entry keyed on the test
fixture would have disarmed the detector on precisely the file that must stay armed — the test
suite for the secret screen. That is a fail-open, and it is invisible: the scan just says clean.

**Generalizable rule for this repo:** prefer removing the literal (assemble credential-shaped
strings at runtime, the discipline `_fake_secret` already established in this suite) over adding
a `.gitleaks.toml` entry. Reach for the allowlist only when the exempted shape is provably not
the first match masking a later one.

PS2 takes the remove-the-literal route for both files: `_pem_banner()` assembles the banner at
runtime in the test, and the module comment abbreviates the banner rather than quoting it in
full. Verified on the PS2 tree: **zero** gitleaks findings, and a throwaway key pasted into
EITHER file is still **DETECTED**. Clean without a single allowlist entry.

### Finding 2 — `bugfix-size-attestation` (502 non-test lines, no attestation)

Remedied as a ticket action, not a code change; the change was NOT split to slip under the
150-line floor. This ticket's description was brought up to date with what implementation
actually proved, then reviewed:

- the seam correction is now IN THE PLAN, not just in a comment — `append_event` is not the
  single write seam, because `_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py:258-276` writes
  Jira-sourced (untrusted, external) bodies by calling the halves of `finalize_event` directly;
  the screen therefore lives at `_seam.finalize_event` (`_commands/_seam.py:329`);
- the refuse-vs-redact ambiguity ("rejects (or redacts, per config)") is replaced by the
  operator's REFUSE + audited-override ruling, with its rationale;
- AC3 / half of AC4 are recorded as ALREADY satisfied on main by bug 2a76 rather than restated
  as new work — the review independently flagged the stale claim, which corroborates the edit;
- added `## Context / Problem`, `## Approach`, `## Scope`, `## Testing`, and citations for every
  asserted capability.

`rebar review-plan e7a9` → **PASS**, attestation signed; `--status` reports `certified`.
Zero blocking findings. Two advisories, both non-blocking and recorded here rather than
actioned: one AC line bundles two deliverables with "and" (P6), and the plan does not state why
a bespoke pattern table is used instead of depending on gitleaks/detect-secrets at the write
seam (T1) — the answer being that the screen must be a pure, offline, in-process function on the
synchronous write path.

# Store accepts secret-bearing event bodies; leak blocked all tickets pushes

## Context / Problem

At 2026-08-03 19:13 an agent session posted a comment on ticket 129e containing a full zsh
environment dump. The dump embedded SEVEN live credentials (Anthropic, 2x GitHub PAT,
Gemini/Google, Jira/Atlassian, OpenAI service-account, PyPI). GitHub push protection then
rejected `refs/heads/tickets` (GH013) on the Anthropic key, so EVERY session's store writes
queued local-only — 153 commits at diagnosis. One comment caused a full store-sharing outage
for all concurrent agents, and it presented as transient contention: the only symptom was
`WARNING rebar._store.push: tickets branch push failed after 3 retries`.

This is urgent now because the store auto-pushes to a single shared ref, so any agent that
pastes an environment dump into a comment wedges the branch for everyone until a human
intervenes.

## Root cause

There is no content screening anywhere in the write path. `_store/event_append._validate_event`
(`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:126`) checks the envelope shape and `event_type` membership
only, and never inspects `data`. Confirmed RED before any fix: `leaf.comment(<ticket>,
"KEY=<live-shaped anthropic key>")` returns 0 and the COMMENT event lands on disk.

Corollary the original diagnosis got wrong, and which this plan corrects: `append_event` is NOT
the single write seam. `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py:258-276` writes
Jira-sourced COMMENT/EDIT bodies — untrusted EXTERNAL input — by calling the halves of
`finalize_event` directly, deliberately bypassing `append_event` because that helper
commits+pushes eagerly. The txn and delete cores bypass it too. A screen at `append_event` would
therefore have left a credential pasted into a Jira comment able to reproduce this exact wedge.

## Approach

Add a deterministic, pure secret screen and enforce it at `_seam.finalize_event`
(`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:329`) — the one function `append_event`
(`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:405`), the txn/delete cores, and the reconciler's inbound
translate all route through. Inbound translate is changed to call the seam rather than its
halves, and a test pins that routing so it cannot regress into a bypass again.

On a match the write is REFUSED — the event does not land — per the operator decision recorded
on this ticket (2026-08-07). Redaction was considered and rejected: silently rewriting a
caller's payload makes the stored event differ from what the caller believes it wrote, and in an
append-only store that divergence is unrecoverable after the fact. Refusal is loud, reversible,
and leaves the caller in control. A force override (`--allow-secret-pattern=<reason>`) keeps a
false positive from ever being a permanent hard block; it is the same escape-hatch shape as
`--force-close`, is CLI-only (never exposed over MCP), and records who forced and why on the
event itself so a forced write is auditable.

Refusal must be safe to leave ON by default, which drives two design constraints:

- It names WHICH family fired and WHERE (field + line), so using the override is an informed
  choice rather than a blind retry.
- It never echoes the secret. `SecretFinding` (`src/rebar/secret_screen.py:116`) carries
  family/field/line and structurally has NO value field, so the value cannot leak through the
  refusal message, logs, stderr, or the event on disk. Payload dict KEYS are redacted before
  they reach the printed field path, since a credential used as a key would otherwise leak
  through the path itself.

Detection is tuned by measurement against the live store rather than by argument. Patterns match
a FIXED-WIDTH window rather than a greedy `{80,}` quantifier, so same-class padding appended
after a real key (400 `-` characters — an ASCII rule in a log or env dump) cannot dilute the
entropy average below the floor and make the screen miss a genuine credential. The PEM pattern is
line-anchored, because a real paste puts the banner on its own line whereas prose enumerating
banners does not.

`llm/workflow/lint.py` consumes the shared pattern table instead of keeping a second copy, which
had already drifted — it lacked the Anthropic/OpenAI/Atlassian/PyPI families the incident
actually carried.

## Scope

Recorded via `set-file-impact` (paths). New: `src/rebar/secret_screen.py` (pattern table, pure
`scan_text`/`screen_event_data`, override audit record, refusal message) and
`tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py`. Modified: `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py` (enforce at
`finalize_event`), `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py` (parse the override above BOTH dispatch
routes so every write verb honours it, not just `comment`), `src/rebar/_commands/leaf.py` and
`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` (thread the override through), `src/rebar/llm/workflow/lint.py`
(consume the shared table), `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py` (route
through the seam), `docs/user-guide.md` (the command-substitution hazard + the screen/override).

Out of scope: surfacing the GH013 push-rejection detail. That was bug 2a76 and already landed on
main (`tests/unit/test_push_rejection_surfacing.py`); AC5 below records it rather than
duplicating it.

## Testing

- Fire: each of the families the incident dump carried is refused, asserted via the family name
  in the refusal. Credential-shaped fixtures are ASSEMBLED AT RUNTIME (`_fake_secret`,
  `_pem_banner`) so this repo never commits a live-shaped literal and the repo's own secret
  scanner stays fully armed on the test file.
- No-fire: the verbatim benign strings the live-store sweep found — a truncated placeholder
  (`sk-ant-api03-...`), a regex literal (`sk-ant-api03-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{93,}`), and prose
  enumerating PEM banners — all still write.
- Padding: a real key followed by 400 same-class padding characters is still refused (the
  fixed-width-window regression).
- No-echo: the secret value AND its head/tail fragments are absent from five channels — the
  exception message, stdout, stderr, the log records, and every byte on disk. The forced-write
  path is checked separately because it is the only path that logs, so asserting on log records
  in the refusal path alone would be vacuous. A positive control proves the on-disk assertion
  can actually observe a landed value.
- Bypass: a test pins that the reconciler's inbound translate routes through `finalize_event`,
  and another pins that the override is absent from the MCP surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A write whose event data matches a high-confidence credential pattern is REFUSED at
      `_seam.finalize_event` and the event file does not exist on disk afterwards — verified by
      a test that asserts the command's non-zero exit and the absence of the event.
- [x] The refusal names the matched secret family and the field+line, and does NOT echo the
      secret value — verified by asserting the value and its head/tail fragments are absent from
      the exception message, stdout, stderr, log records, and all on-disk bytes.
- [x] Benign look-alike text (truncated placeholders, regex literals, prose enumerating
      banners — the verbatim strings from the live-store sweep) still writes successfully, so
      the screen is safe to leave on by default — verified by explicit negative-case tests.
- [x] The screen covers writers that do NOT go through `append_event`, specifically the
      reconciler's inbound Jira translate — verified by a test asserting inbound translate
      routes through `finalize_event`.
- [x] `--allow-secret-pattern=<reason>` allows the refused write for every write verb, records
      the reason and bypassed families on the event, and is absent from the MCP tool surface —
      verified by tests over the CLI verbs and a test asserting MCP non-exposure.
- [x] The shell command-substitution hazard that produced the incident is documented in
      `docs/user-guide.md` with the exact wrong and right forms.
- [x] The incident is recorded on this ticket with its blast radius, including that the only
      control which actually stopped the leak (GitHub push protection) was outside this project.
- [x] Surfacing the GH013 push-rejection reason is confirmed ALREADY satisfied on main by bug
      2a76 (`tests/unit/test_push_rejection_surfacing.py`) and is not duplicated here.

## Absorbed from e4f4 (closed as duplicate)

e4f4-295b-2c03-44c4 described the same underlying defect (the store accepting secret-bearing
event bodies) and was filed about 8 minutes apart from this ticket with no link between them.
Its two ACs with no counterpart here — documenting the shell command-substitution hazard for
agents, and recording the incident with its blast radius — are folded into the Acceptance
Criteria above so nothing is lost by closing it.

file_impact.reason: New: the pattern table, the pure scan_text/screen_event_data detector, the override audit record, and the refusal message.
Enforce the screen at finalize_event (the one seam every writer shares) + the forced_secret_write override scope.
Parse --allow-secret-pattern=<reason> above both dispatch routes so every write verb honours it.
Thread allow_secret_pattern through the library comment() wrapper.
Consume the shared pattern table instead of keeping a second, drifting copy.
Route inbound Jira events through finalize_event so they are screened (was a bypass).
Document the shell command-substitution hazard and the screen + override.
